newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan applauds Clinton, seeks active U.S. role.
newsitem.headline: Jordan applauds Clinton, seeks active U.S. role.

text.p: Jordan applauded on Wednesday U.S. President Bill Clinton's re-election but called for a more active U.S. role to rescue Middle East peace talks from crisis.

"We welcome Mr Clinton's re-election," Information Minister Marwan Muasher said. "We think he has been very instrumental in pushing the peace process forward and we hope he will do even more in terms of getting the peace process out of its present crisis.
"We think that his re-election opens the door for a more active role by the U.S. and we would welcome this," Muasher told Reuters.
U.S.-sponsored Israeli-Palestinian talks are deadlocked over implementation of an Israeli troop pullback in the West Bank town of Hebron, home to 400 Jewish settlers and 100,000 Palestinians.

Jordan's relations with Israel, built on a 1994 peace treaty which ended a 46-year state of war, soured in September when the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu opened a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem, angering King Hussein who was granted a custodial role over the sites in the 1994 accord.
